Explanation:  
The question asks for the century in which the current name of the Dutch equivalent of the September Declaration (Prinsjesdag) was chosen. The Ground Truth Answer is "the 19th century". The Predicted Answer explains that while the term “Prinsjesdag” originated in the 18th century for a different purpose (the birthday of Prince William V), it specifies that the name began to be applied to the parliamentary opening ceremony—i.e., its "current" use—in the 19th century. Therefore, the vital information in the Ground Truth Answer ("19th century") is indeed present in the Predicted Answer.
